what: The Email Signature Generator makes a professional signature for your emails. Type your name, job title, company, phone, email, website and address, add a photo or logo and links to your social profiles, and see the result in a live email preview.

Choose from five layouts: Photo left, Divider, Stacked, Banner and Compact. Set an accent colour, an email-safe font and the text size. The signature is built from simple tables and inline styles, so it looks the same in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail.
Press Copy signature to copy it with its formatting, then paste it into your email settings. Instructions for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail and phone apps are right below the preview.
uses: Give every email a clear name, job title and contact details.
Add your logo, website and a "Book a call" or "Shop now" button.
Link to your portfolio and professional profiles.
Make matching signatures for everyone by changing only the names and numbers.
Use a simple signature with your phone and profile link when you apply for jobs.
tutorial: Fill in your name, job title, company, phone, email, website and, if you like, your address.
Paste a link to a picture that is already online (starting with https://). Uploading also works, but some email apps remove uploaded pictures.
Add social links and a button
Type your profile addresses or usernames. For a button, add both the button text and its link.
Choose a layout, then set the accent colour, font and text size. The preview updates straight away.
Press Copy signature. It copies the formatted signature, with a plain text version for apps that need one.
Paste it into your email app
Pick your app in the tabs under the preview and follow the steps, then send yourself a test email.
features: Photo left, Divider, Stacked, Banner and Compact.
Table-based HTML with inline styles that Gmail and Outlook keep.
Copies rich formatting, plus the HTML code if you need it.
LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, GitHub and a call-to-action button.
Only web, email and phone links are added, so the signature cannot break or carry scripts.
Steps for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail and phone apps.
Come back later and your signature is still there.

example.title: Worked example: a signature for Gmail
example.text: Priya types her name, "Head of Customer Success", Brightline Labs, her phone, email and website, and pastes the link to her photo from the company website. She adds her LinkedIn address and a "Book a call" button linking to her calendar. She picks the Divider layout in blue, presses Copy signature, opens Gmail settings, pastes it into a new signature and saves. Her next email shows the photo, links and button.

tips: Keep it short: name, role, one or two ways to contact you and a link is enough.
Host pictures online and paste the https:// link so they show for every recipient.
Send a test email to yourself and to a friend on a different email app.
Use your accent colour from your logo or website for a matching look.
Avoid putting important text inside images; some apps block images until the reader allows them.
problems: The pasted signature has no formatting
Paste with Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on Mac), not "paste as plain text". If your app still strips it, use "Copy HTML code" if the app accepts HTML.
The photo shows as a broken image
The link must point straight at the picture file and start with https://. Open the link in a new tab: it should show only the picture.
Some browsers block copying. Select the preview with your mouse, copy it with Ctrl+C, then paste.
The layout looks different on a phone
Phone apps often use a plain text signature. The full design shows in emails you send from your computer or webmail.
